videos.title: Vacationing in Granby, Colorado this week and doing plenty of birding while I'm here! One bird kept
videos.description:
Vacationing in Granby, Colorado this week and doing plenty of birding while I'm here! One bird kept singing from a riverside bush and stumped my Merlin app for days. When I finally got him on video and uploaded a photo, Merlin identified him as a Western Flycatcher, a bird with some behaviors similar to our Eastern Phoebe back home in Omaha, but a completely different species suited to a completely different part of the country. Such a fun reminder of how much your local bird list changes with the landscape.

videos.description:
Stop Window Strikes: Protect Backyard Birds with Window Gems 🪟🐦

Day 5 of our migration station series tackles one of the biggest threats to backyard birds: window strikes. When sunlight hits glass at certain angles, it reflects the sky and birds don't see the barrier, leading to injury, predator attacks, or death.

Window gems are reusable window clings that act like a stop sign for birds, breaking up that reflection so they know to avoid it. They last for years and come in packs of seven with designs like bears, birds, raccoons, squirrels, and eagles.

videos.title: Late Summer Bird Feeder Cleaning: Stop Mold and Buildup Before Migration Season
videos.description:
Late Summer Bird Feeder Cleaning: Stop Mold and Buildup Before Migration Season

Rain during late summer can leave your bird feeders covered in mold and gunk, and it's enough to turn birds away entirely. Here's how we deep clean every feeder in our yard: spray with white vinegar and let it sit, soak in hot water with Dawn dish soap, then scrub thoroughly.

Best tools for the job: a Scrub Daddy for bird baths, a double ended bottle brush for hummingbird feeders, a mascara style brush for small holes, and a long tube scrubber for tube feeders.

We also simplify our seed to a high quality blend without fillers, and add some cover to the yard to help birds feel safe as they prep for migration.

Migratory birds molting this fall need secure cover to hide from predators. Today's tips: leave brush piles and small trees intact, cover your feeders with branches or a shelter overhead, and know that by October birds will be fully molted and better equipped to evade predators.

videos.title: Fall Bird Migration Tips: How to turn your yard into a migration pit stop for traveling birds 🍂🐦
videos.description:
Fall Bird Migration Tips: How to turn your yard into a migration pit stop for traveling birds 🍂🐦

Step 1 of transforming your backyard for migration season: streamline your feeder menu with high quality, reliable food.

Choose fresh black oil sunflower seed, or a mix with nuts, safflower, and fruit, and skip filler seeds like millet and cracked corn this time of year. Try a no filler patio blend (just black oil sunflower and peanut pieces), or set up an all peanut tube feeder to attract woodpeckers, chickadees, nuthatches, and cardinals. Molting birds need extra nutritional support too!

Stay tuned for the next step in transforming your backyard into a migration haven.

videos.title: Ruby-throated hummingbirds are swarming feeders across the country right now, and our friend Sherry
videos.description:
Ruby-throated hummingbirds are swarming feeders across the country right now, and our friend Sherry in Mt. Olive, Arkansas is going through almost 8 cups of nectar a day to keep up. 🐦

These tiny birds are prepping for an incredible journey. Starting in late July, they enter "hyperphagia" and nearly double their body weight on nectar and insects. Many then fly nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico for 18 to 22 hours with no chance to stop and refuel. Others take the coastal route through Texas and Mexico. By winter, most ruby-throats have made it to somewhere between southern Mexico and Panama.

Keep your feeders full this time of year, they need the fuel for the trip ahead!

videos.description:
It's molting season, which means your backyard birds are "changing their clothes" 🪶 and staying extra hidden because they're more vulnerable to predators right now. Here's how we help ground feeders like cardinals and doves stay safe during this quiet stretch: we bring the ground up to them! This hanging tray feeder is loaded with a Flaming Hot Feast cake, a mini suet ball, and a sprinkle of safflower, then covered for extra safety. Hang it near a tree or bush for a quick escape route and watch them feel right at home.
